vertical_schema.title: Job search: Japanese staffing and employment
vertical_schema.description: Synthetic job-search vocabulary for Japanese employment listings. All examples are illustrative sampling seeds, not verified vacancies. Missing evidence must not be inferred.

x-adaptgym.scope: Synthetic Japan / JPY job-search benchmark; no partner feed data

simulation.label: Job search
simulation.domain_instructions: Simulate a job seeker finding suitable Japanese job listings. Pay is in JPY; hourly and monthly pay must not be compared or converted. A positive ending means finding a suitable opportunity or shortlist, not applying, receiving an offer, or being hired. Selecting a listing alone does not complete the search. Candidate skills and experience are capabilities, not preferences for jobs requiring those skills. Staffing agency is distinct from the client employer. remote_negotiable is not guaranteed remote or hybrid. unspecified and omitted fields are unknown evidence, not negative facts. Required and mentioned skills are distinct. Overtime limits need a known reference period before comparing periods.
service_questions: Application steps are not available in this synthetic catalog.
Recruiter contact details are not available in this synthetic catalog.
Interview details are not available in this synthetic catalog.

job_title.description: Actual position title, preserving specializations; do not replace it with a promotional feed headline.
job_title.title: the kind of job you want

category_breadcrumb.description: Partner breadcrumb as a single normalized path; equality compares the full path, not ancestors.
examples: Kyoto / Temporary staffing / General office work

location_country.description: ISO country code explicitly supplied by the listing.

location_region.description: Normalized prefecture name; examples are sampling seeds, not an exhaustive vocabulary.
location_region.title: the prefecture

location_locality.description: Normalized municipality and ward; keep compatible with the region when constructing listings.
location_locality.title: the city or ward

short_description.description: Concise factual summary from the full page or JSON-LD description. A workweek alone is not a job summary.

employer_name.description: Actual employer, when explicitly identified; unspecified otherwise. Keep the employer distinct from a recruiting or staffing agency.

staffing_agency.description: Recruiting or staffing organization, distinct from the client employer.

salary_hourly_jpy.description: Explicitly advertised hourly pay in JPY. If quoted as a range or lower bound, retain the guaranteed lower endpoint; omit when unknown. Never derive it from monthly pay.
salary_hourly_jpy.title: hourly pay in JPY

salary_monthly_jpy.description: Explicitly advertised monthly pay in JPY; retain the lower endpoint of a range or lower-bound quote. Omit if not stated; do not convert hourly pay.

employment_type.description: Normalized illustrative employment categories, kept distinct from hours worked.
employment_type.title: the employment contract type

working_days_pattern.description: Explicit workweek pattern; unspecified if missing. A weekday schedule alone does not establish intraday hours.

days_per_week.description: Explicit number of working days each week; omit if unknown.
days_per_week.title: working days per week

work_start_minute.description: Local start time as minutes after midnight, e.g. 540 = 09:00. Omit when unknown.
work_start_minute.title: the earliest acceptable start time

work_end_minute.description: Local end time as minutes after midnight, e.g. 1060 = 17:40. Omit when unknown. Overnight shifts need explicit handling outside this schema.
work_end_minute.title: the latest acceptable finish time

working_minutes_per_day.description: Explicit paid/actual daily working duration, not a duration inferred from clock times. Preserve source discrepancies for review.

break_minutes_per_day.description: Explicit break duration; omit if not stated.

shorter_hours_negotiable.description: Whether the listing explicitly permits discussing shorter hours. Missing evidence is unspecified.
shorter_hours_negotiable.title: whether reduced hours must be negotiable

work_arrangement.description: Explicit work arrangement. remote_negotiable means work from home can be discussed, not guaranteed remote or hybrid work. Never infer on-site from an occupation.

minimum_experience_months.description: Explicit minimum required experience; omit when unknown. Do not translate an occupation label into a numeric requirement.
minimum_experience_months.title: experience required by the job, in months

experience_specialization.description: Explicit required experience, separate from duration. unspecified if missing.

teacher_forced.extractor_prompt:
Extract current intent using only the visible two-way conversation and schema.
Return intent as a short natural-language string summarizing the current user goal.
For example: "Find suitable listings matching the current requirements." It must agree with the structured claims
and search request. Update this summary from the latest turn; do not carry an earlier search goal
forward unchanged after completion. In particular:
- "I didn't find what I wanted, so I'll stop searching" => "The user rejected the results and
  stopped searching without finding what they wanted." active_task_id=null, claims contain no task
  requirements, search_request=null, satisfied=false; retain any previously identified selected_products.
- "I found what I wanted, I'm done" => summarize satisfied completion, not an ongoing search.
- Rejecting results while asking to keep looking is NOT completion; summarize the continuing search.
Never use an imperative summary like "Find suitable listings" for a task the user has stopped.
Return all active hard requirements and soft preferences, keeping task and durable scope separate.
Use task-1 for the first search task, task-2 for the next, and so on. Use null when no task is active.
Scope may be unknown when not established. Durable and unknown-scope claims have null task_id.
Resolve confirmations and product references using assistant context, but never treat an assistant suggestion alone as user evidence.
Preserve unrelated requirements when revising a value. Clear temporary requirements at task boundaries. A statement such as "I've found exactly what I
wanted; I'm finished looking" closes the task: active_task_id=null, task claims removed,
selected_products retains the identified product. Preserve durable preferences. Mere politeness is not necessarily completion.
Choosing a product alone does NOT close the search task. For "I'll take the second one", keep
active_task_id=task-1 and existing task claims with task_id=task-1, set selected_products to a list containing the chosen
ID, search_request=null, and satisfied="unk". Only a later expressed completion clears active_task_id
and task-scoped claims. Never output active_task_id=null while retaining task-scoped claims.
Represent a product choice only as selected_products; do not infer all its attributes as durable preferences.
Cite real message IDs in evidence; include the assistant question/list when necessary, and the user's support.
Return value as the actual typed scalar or membership array, never as JSON encoded inside a string. Use schema operators and units.
Also extract satisfied as true for expressed success, false for expressed failure, or "unk" when
not established (including silence). Do not infer satisfaction just from recommendations or selection.
selected_products is the list of catalog IDs the user explicitly chose; [] if unspecified.
Discussing or liking an item alone is not a selection.
Retain that product through task completion. Reset both
outcome fields when a new task begins. Never invent a product because the user says "found it".
The previous prediction is fallible: correct it using the conversation if necessary.
Also emit search_request as part of the intent: {query, filters, preferences}.
query must be a useful, nonempty natural-language search phrase naming the item
category and known needs. Refine the phrase as more needs become known. Never output placeholders such as "/", "*", or schema field names alone. filters contain ALL active hard requirements;
preferences contain soft preferences, never hard filters. Each uses attribute/operator/typed value.
Use the current task's value when it overrides a durable preference on the same attribute. Unknown
scope or strength stays in claims for clarification, not in automatic search constraints.
Return null if there is no active task or a product has already been selected. Selection lookup is
not a new catalog search. Never put unsupported constraints into query text. Emit active claims only, not superseded values. No private plan or expected states are available.
Also return target_products as the list of catalog IDs the USER explicitly expressed interest in.
Assistant recommendations alone never establish interest. Add IDs after an explicit expression
of interest; remove IDs when the user withdraws interest. Selecting an item also expresses interest.
Keep selected_products separate: interest alone is not a selection and does not stop search.
Resolve positions using the assistant's actual displayed order. Use [] when no interest or selection
has been expressed. Keep selections within target_products. Reset both lists when a new task begins.
Also return preferences as a list of {preferred: catalog_ID, over: catalog_ID} pairs.
"I prefer X over Y" means X > Y. "I prefer X" in an unambiguous displayed comparison
means X > each of the other compared alternatives. Resolve the comparison set from the
user's reference and assistant context; do not compare against every item ever shown.
"I like X" alone establishes interest, not relative preference. A comparison request alone
establishes neither. Preference adds X to target_products but does not select X or reject Y.
Do NOT add Y to target_products merely because it is compared or liked LESS than X.
A request to compare X and Y alone does NOT add either to target_products.
Keep Y as a target only if the user separately expressed interest in Y.
Preserve earlier pairs, replace a reversed pair when the user revises it, and reset preferences
on a new task. Do not invent transitive pairs or infer durable attribute preferences.
Intent contract:
- Attribute requirements and durable attribute preferences belong in claims. An attribute preference
  (e.g. generally preferring a brand or work arrangement) NEVER creates an item-to-item ranking.
- target_products is an explicitly endorsed shortlist of catalog ENTRY IDs, not all eligible items.
  Asking for a comparison, mentioning a model, or requiring its attributes does not endorse an entry,
  even if only one catalog entry currently matches. Catalog descriptions alone establish no user facts.
- selected_products requires an explicit choice of a catalog entry, not mere liking or preference.
  Selection alone neither completes a task nor establishes satisfaction.
- preferences contains only directed {preferred: catalog-entry-ID, over: catalog-entry-ID} pairs.
  "I prefer the first one" after a clear comparison ranks it above the other compared entries.
  It endorses that entry without selecting it or rejecting the others. Attribute values are never IDs.
- Withdrawing interest removes only the identified entry from the shortlist/selection. It does not
  retract a model, brand or other attribute requirement unless the user separately says so. Wording
  must distinguish a particular listing from the model or class of items. New tasks reset item state.
- satisfied describes the overall task outcome: true for explicit overall success, false for explicit
  overall failure, and "unk" if not established. Rejecting one recommendation while continuing the
  search does not by itself establish an overall failure. Never infer an outcome from assistant tone.
- Do not require redundant re-encodings of the same fact in additional_intent. For example,
  a captured specific sport need does not also require an equivalent category label. A new sport
  mentioned in the conversation is still missing if the candidate records only a surface.
  An explicitly stated intended use that already names the activity (e.g. primary_use=Sprinting)
  captures that activity; do not demand an additional sport=sprinting claim for the same fact.
  A road surface alone, however, does not establish road running rather than walking.
- Labels must cover ALL current schema-defined intent established by the visible USER conversation,
  including unambiguous implications. Do not invent constraints from persona background, a matching
  catalog entry, or an assistant's suggestion. Retire task claims on completion; retain durable claims.

rollout.extractor_prompt:
Extract current intent using only the visible two-way conversation and schema.
Return intent as a short natural-language string summarizing the current user goal.
For example: "Find suitable listings matching the current requirements." It must agree with the structured claims
and search request. Update this summary from the latest turn; do not carry an earlier search goal
forward unchanged after completion. In particular:
- "I didn't find what I wanted, so I'll stop searching" => "The user rejected the results and
  stopped searching without finding what they wanted." active_task_id=null, claims contain no task
  requirements, search_request=null, satisfied=false; retain any previously identified selected_products.
- "I found what I wanted, I'm done" => summarize satisfied completion, not an ongoing search.
- Rejecting results while asking to keep looking is NOT completion; summarize the continuing search.
Never use an imperative summary like "Find suitable listings" for a task the user has stopped.
Return all active hard requirements and soft preferences, keeping task and durable scope separate.
Use task-1 for the first search task, task-2 for the next, and so on. Use null when no task is active.
Scope may be unknown when not established. Durable and unknown-scope claims have null task_id.
Resolve confirmations and product references using assistant context, but never treat an assistant suggestion alone as user evidence.
Preserve unrelated requirements when revising a value. Clear temporary requirements at task boundaries. A statement such as "I've found exactly what I
wanted; I'm finished looking" closes the task: active_task_id=null, task claims removed,
selected_products retains the identified product. Preserve durable preferences. Mere politeness is not necessarily completion.
Choosing a product alone does NOT close the search task. For "I'll take the second one", keep
active_task_id=task-1 and existing task claims with task_id=task-1, set selected_products to a list containing the chosen
ID, search_request=null, and satisfied="unk". Only a later expressed completion clears active_task_id
and task-scoped claims. Never output active_task_id=null while retaining task-scoped claims.
Represent a product choice only as selected_products; do not infer all its attributes as durable preferences.
Cite real message IDs in evidence; include the assistant question/list when necessary, and the user's support.
Return value as the actual typed scalar or membership array, never as JSON encoded inside a string. Use schema operators and units.
Also extract satisfied as true for expressed success, false for expressed failure, or "unk" when
not established (including silence). Do not infer satisfaction just from recommendations or selection.
selected_products is the list of catalog IDs the user explicitly chose; [] if unspecified.
Discussing or liking an item alone is not a selection.
Retain that product through task completion. Reset both
outcome fields when a new task begins. Never invent a product because the user says "found it".
The previous prediction is fallible: correct it using the conversation if necessary.
Also emit search_request as part of the intent: {query, filters, preferences}.
query must be a useful, nonempty natural-language search phrase naming the item
category and known needs. Refine the phrase as more needs become known. Never output placeholders such as "/", "*", or schema field names alone. filters contain ALL active hard requirements;
preferences contain soft preferences, never hard filters. Each uses attribute/operator/typed value.
Use the current task's value when it overrides a durable preference on the same attribute. Unknown
scope or strength stays in claims for clarification, not in automatic search constraints.
Return null if there is no active task or a product has already been selected. Selection lookup is
not a new catalog search. Never put unsupported constraints into query text. Emit active claims only, not superseded values. No private plan or expected states are available.
Also return target_products as the list of catalog IDs the USER explicitly expressed interest in.
Assistant recommendations alone never establish interest. Add IDs after an explicit expression
of interest; remove IDs when the user withdraws interest. Selecting an item also expresses interest.
Keep selected_products separate: interest alone is not a selection and does not stop search.
Resolve positions using the assistant's actual displayed order. Use [] when no interest or selection
has been expressed. Keep selections within target_products. Reset both lists when a new task begins.
Also return preferences as a list of {preferred: catalog_ID, over: catalog_ID} pairs.
"I prefer X over Y" means X > Y. "I prefer X" in an unambiguous displayed comparison
means X > each of the other compared alternatives. Resolve the comparison set from the
user's reference and assistant context; do not compare against every item ever shown.
"I like X" alone establishes interest, not relative preference. A comparison request alone
establishes neither. Preference adds X to target_products but does not select X or reject Y.
Do NOT add Y to target_products merely because it is compared or liked LESS than X.
A request to compare X and Y alone does NOT add either to target_products.
Keep Y as a target only if the user separately expressed interest in Y.
Preserve earlier pairs, replace a reversed pair when the user revises it, and reset preferences
on a new task. Do not invent transitive pairs or infer durable attribute preferences.
Intent contract:
- Attribute requirements and durable attribute preferences belong in claims. An attribute preference
  (e.g. generally preferring a brand or work arrangement) NEVER creates an item-to-item ranking.
- target_products is an explicitly endorsed shortlist of catalog ENTRY IDs, not all eligible items.
  Asking for a comparison, mentioning a model, or requiring its attributes does not endorse an entry,
  even if only one catalog entry currently matches. Catalog descriptions alone establish no user facts.
- selected_products requires an explicit choice of a catalog entry, not mere liking or preference.
  Selection alone neither completes a task nor establishes satisfaction.
- preferences contains only directed {preferred: catalog-entry-ID, over: catalog-entry-ID} pairs.
  "I prefer the first one" after a clear comparison ranks it above the other compared entries.
  It endorses that entry without selecting it or rejecting the others. Attribute values are never IDs.
- Withdrawing interest removes only the identified entry from the shortlist/selection. It does not
  retract a model, brand or other attribute requirement unless the user separately says so. Wording
  must distinguish a particular listing from the model or class of items. New tasks reset item state.
- satisfied describes the overall task outcome: true for explicit overall success, false for explicit
  overall failure, and "unk" if not established. Rejecting one recommendation while continuing the
  search does not by itself establish an overall failure. Never infer an outcome from assistant tone.
- Do not require redundant re-encodings of the same fact in additional_intent. For example,
  a captured specific sport need does not also require an equivalent category label. A new sport
  mentioned in the conversation is still missing if the candidate records only a surface.
  An explicitly stated intended use that already names the activity (e.g. primary_use=Sprinting)
  captures that activity; do not demand an additional sport=sprinting claim for the same fact.
  A road surface alone, however, does not establish road running rather than walking.
- Labels must cover ALL current schema-defined intent established by the visible USER conversation,
  including unambiguous implications. Do not invent constraints from persona background, a matching
  catalog entry, or an assistant's suggestion. Retire task claims on completion; retain durable claims.

teacher_forced.label: Qwen 4B zero-shot
teacher_forced.extractor_prompt:
Extract current intent using only the visible two-way conversation and schema.
Return intent as a short natural-language string summarizing the current user goal.
For example: "Find suitable listings matching the current requirements." It must agree with the structured claims
and search request. Update this summary from the latest turn; do not carry an earlier search goal
forward unchanged after completion. In particular:
- "I didn't find what I wanted, so I'll stop searching" => "The user rejected the results and
  stopped searching without finding what they wanted." active_task_id=null, claims contain no task
  requirements, search_request=null, satisfied=false; retain any previously identified selected_products.
- "I found what I wanted, I'm done" => summarize satisfied completion, not an ongoing search.
- Rejecting results while asking to keep looking is NOT completion; summarize the continuing search.
Never use an imperative summary like "Find suitable listings" for a task the user has stopped.
Return all active hard requirements and soft preferences, keeping task and durable scope separate.
Use task-1 for the first search task, task-2 for the next, and so on. Use null when no task is active.
Scope may be unknown when not established. Durable and unknown-scope claims have null task_id.
Resolve confirmations and product references using assistant context, but never treat an assistant suggestion alone as user evidence.
Preserve unrelated requirements when revising a value. Clear temporary requirements at task boundaries. A statement such as "I've found exactly what I
wanted; I'm finished looking" closes the task: active_task_id=null, task claims removed,
selected_products retains the identified product. Preserve durable preferences. Mere politeness is not necessarily completion.
Choosing a product alone does NOT close the search task. For "I'll take the second one", keep
active_task_id=task-1 and existing task claims with task_id=task-1, set selected_products to a list containing the chosen
ID, search_request=null, and satisfied="unk". Only a later expressed completion clears active_task_id
and task-scoped claims. Never output active_task_id=null while retaining task-scoped claims.
Represent a product choice only as selected_products; do not infer all its attributes as durable preferences.
Cite real message IDs in evidence; include the assistant question/list when necessary, and the user's support.
Return value as the actual typed scalar or membership array, never as JSON encoded inside a string. Use schema operators and units.
Also extract satisfied as true for expressed success, false for expressed failure, or "unk" when
not established (including silence). Do not infer satisfaction just from recommendations or selection.
selected_products is the list of catalog IDs the user explicitly chose; [] if unspecified.
Discussing or liking an item alone is not a selection.
Retain that product through task completion. Reset both
outcome fields when a new task begins. Never invent a product because the user says "found it".
The previous prediction is fallible: correct it using the conversation if necessary.
Also emit search_request as part of the intent: {query, filters, preferences}.
query must be a useful, nonempty natural-language search phrase naming the item
category and known needs. Refine the phrase as more needs become known. Never output placeholders such as "/", "*", or schema field names alone. filters contain ALL active hard requirements;
preferences contain soft preferences, never hard filters. Each uses attribute/operator/typed value.
Use the current task's value when it overrides a durable preference on the same attribute. Unknown
scope or strength stays in claims for clarification, not in automatic search constraints.
Return null if there is no active task or a product has already been selected. Selection lookup is
not a new catalog search. Never put unsupported constraints into query text. Emit active claims only, not superseded values. No private plan or expected states are available.
Also return target_products as the list of catalog IDs the USER explicitly expressed interest in.
Assistant recommendations alone never establish interest. Add IDs after an explicit expression
of interest; remove IDs when the user withdraws interest. Selecting an item also expresses interest.
Keep selected_products separate: interest alone is not a selection and does not stop search.
Resolve positions using the assistant's actual displayed order. Use [] when no interest or selection
has been expressed. Keep selections within target_products. Reset both lists when a new task begins.
Also return preferences as a list of {preferred: catalog_ID, over: catalog_ID} pairs.
"I prefer X over Y" means X > Y. "I prefer X" in an unambiguous displayed comparison
means X > each of the other compared alternatives. Resolve the comparison set from the
user's reference and assistant context; do not compare against every item ever shown.
"I like X" alone establishes interest, not relative preference. A comparison request alone
establishes neither. Preference adds X to target_products but does not select X or reject Y.
Do NOT add Y to target_products merely because it is compared or liked LESS than X.
A request to compare X and Y alone does NOT add either to target_products.
Keep Y as a target only if the user separately expressed interest in Y.
Preserve earlier pairs, replace a reversed pair when the user revises it, and reset preferences
on a new task. Do not invent transitive pairs or infer durable attribute preferences.
Intent contract:
- Attribute requirements and durable attribute preferences belong in claims. An attribute preference
  (e.g. generally preferring a brand or work arrangement) NEVER creates an item-to-item ranking.
- target_products is an explicitly endorsed shortlist of catalog ENTRY IDs, not all eligible items.
  Asking for a comparison, mentioning a model, or requiring its attributes does not endorse an entry,
  even if only one catalog entry currently matches. Catalog descriptions alone establish no user facts.
- selected_products requires an explicit choice of a catalog entry, not mere liking or preference.
  Selection alone neither completes a task nor establishes satisfaction.
- preferences contains only directed {preferred: catalog-entry-ID, over: catalog-entry-ID} pairs.
  "I prefer the first one" after a clear comparison ranks it above the other compared entries.
  It endorses that entry without selecting it or rejecting the others. Attribute values are never IDs.
- Withdrawing interest removes only the identified entry from the shortlist/selection. It does not
  retract a model, brand or other attribute requirement unless the user separately says so. Wording
  must distinguish a particular listing from the model or class of items. New tasks reset item state.
- satisfied describes the overall task outcome: true for explicit overall success, false for explicit
  overall failure, and "unk" if not established. Rejecting one recommendation while continuing the
  search does not by itself establish an overall failure. Never infer an outcome from assistant tone.
- Do not require redundant re-encodings of the same fact in additional_intent. For example,
  a captured specific sport need does not also require an equivalent category label. A new sport
  mentioned in the conversation is still missing if the candidate records only a surface.
  An explicitly stated intended use that already names the activity (e.g. primary_use=Sprinting)
  captures that activity; do not demand an additional sport=sprinting claim for the same fact.
  A road surface alone, however, does not establish road running rather than walking.
- Labels must cover ALL current schema-defined intent established by the visible USER conversation,
  including unambiguous implications. Do not invent constraints from persona background, a matching
  catalog entry, or an assistant's suggestion. Retire task claims on completion; retain durable claims.

  even if only one catalog entry currently matches. Catalog descriptions alone establish no user facts.
- selected_products requires an explicit choice of a catalog entry, not mere liking or preference.
  Selection alone neither completes a task nor establishes satisfaction.
- preferences contains only directed {preferred: catalog-entry-ID, over: catalog-entry-ID} pairs.

  It endorses that entry without selecting it or rejecting the others. Attribute values are never IDs.

teacher_forced.extractor_prompt:
Extract current intent using only the visible two-way conversation and schema.
Return intent as a short natural-language string summarizing the current user goal.
For example: "Find suitable listings matching the current requirements." It must agree with the structured claims
and search request. Update this summary from the latest turn; do not carry an earlier search goal
forward unchanged after completion. In particular:
- "I didn't find what I wanted, so I'll stop searching" => "The user rejected the results and
  stopped searching without finding what they wanted." active_task_id=null, claims contain no task
  requirements, search_request=null, satisfied=false; retain any previously identified selected_products.
- "I found what I wanted, I'm done" => summarize satisfied completion, not an ongoing search.
- Rejecting results while asking to keep looking is NOT completion; summarize the continuing search.
Never use an imperative summary like "Find suitable listings" for a task the user has stopped.
Return all active hard requirements and soft preferences, keeping task and durable scope separate.
Use task-1 for the first search task, task-2 for the next, and so on. Use null when no task is active.
Scope may be unknown when not established. Durable and unknown-scope claims have null task_id.
Resolve confirmations and product references using assistant context, but never treat an assistant suggestion alone as user evidence.
Preserve unrelated requirements when revising a value. Clear temporary requirements at task boundaries. A statement such as "I've found exactly what I
wanted; I'm finished looking" closes the task: active_task_id=null, task claims removed,
selected_products retains the identified product. Preserve durable preferences. Mere politeness is not necessarily completion.
Choosing a product alone does NOT close the search task. For "I'll take the second one", keep
active_task_id=task-1 and existing task claims with task_id=task-1, set selected_products to a list containing the chosen
ID, search_request=null, and satisfied="unk". Only a later expressed completion clears active_task_id
and task-scoped claims. Never output active_task_id=null while retaining task-scoped claims.
Represent a product choice only as selected_products; do not infer all its attributes as durable preferences.
Cite real message IDs in evidence; include the assistant question/list when necessary, and the user's support.
Return value as the actual typed scalar or membership array, never as JSON encoded inside a string. Use schema operators and units.
Also extract satisfied as true for expressed success, false for expressed failure, or "unk" when
not established (including silence). Do not infer satisfaction just from recommendations or selection.
selected_products is the list of catalog IDs the user explicitly chose; [] if unspecified.
Discussing or liking an item alone is not a selection.
Retain that product through task completion. Reset both
outcome fields when a new task begins. Never invent a product because the user says "found it".
The previous prediction is fallible: correct it using the conversation if necessary.
Also emit search_request as part of the intent: {query, filters, preferences}.
query must be a useful, nonempty natural-language search phrase naming the item
category and known needs. Refine the phrase as more needs become known. Never output placeholders such as "/", "*", or schema field names alone. filters contain ALL active hard requirements;
preferences contain soft preferences, never hard filters. Each uses attribute/operator/typed value.
Use the current task's value when it overrides a durable preference on the same attribute. Unknown
scope or strength stays in claims for clarification, not in automatic search constraints.
Return null if there is no active task or a product has already been selected. Selection lookup is
not a new catalog search. Never put unsupported constraints into query text. Emit active claims only, not superseded values. No private plan or expected states are available.
Also return target_products as the list of catalog IDs the USER explicitly expressed interest in.
Assistant recommendations alone never establish interest. Add IDs after an explicit expression
of interest; remove IDs when the user withdraws interest. Selecting an item also expresses interest.
Keep selected_products separate: interest alone is not a selection and does not stop search.
Resolve positions using the assistant's actual displayed order. Use [] when no interest or selection
has been expressed. Keep selections within target_products. Reset both lists when a new task begins.
Also return preferences as a list of {preferred: catalog_ID, over: catalog_ID} pairs.
"I prefer X over Y" means X > Y. "I prefer X" in an unambiguous displayed comparison
means X > each of the other compared alternatives. Resolve the comparison set from the
user's reference and assistant context; do not compare against every item ever shown.
"I like X" alone establishes interest, not relative preference. A comparison request alone
establishes neither. Preference adds X to target_products but does not select X or reject Y.
Do NOT add Y to target_products merely because it is compared or liked LESS than X.
A request to compare X and Y alone does NOT add either to target_products.
Keep Y as a target only if the user separately expressed interest in Y.
Preserve earlier pairs, replace a reversed pair when the user revises it, and reset preferences
on a new task. Do not invent transitive pairs or infer durable attribute preferences.
Intent contract:
- Attribute requirements and durable attribute preferences belong in claims. An attribute preference
  (e.g. generally preferring a brand or work arrangement) NEVER creates an item-to-item ranking.
- target_products is an explicitly endorsed shortlist of catalog ENTRY IDs, not all eligible items.
  Asking for a comparison, mentioning a model, or requiring its attributes does not endorse an entry,
  even if only one catalog entry currently matches. Catalog descriptions alone establish no user facts.
- selected_products requires an explicit choice of a catalog entry, not mere liking or preference.
  Selection alone neither completes a task nor establishes satisfaction.
- preferences contains only directed {preferred: catalog-entry-ID, over: catalog-entry-ID} pairs.
  "I prefer the first one" after a clear comparison ranks it above the other compared entries.
  It endorses that entry without selecting it or rejecting the others. Attribute values are never IDs.
- Withdrawing interest removes only the identified entry from the shortlist/selection. It does not
  retract a model, brand or other attribute requirement unless the user separately says so. Wording
  must distinguish a particular listing from the model or class of items. New tasks reset item state.
- satisfied describes the overall task outcome: true for explicit overall success, false for explicit
  overall failure, and "unk" if not established. Rejecting one recommendation while continuing the
  search does not by itself establish an overall failure. Never infer an outcome from assistant tone.
- Do not require redundant re-encodings of the same fact in additional_intent. For example,
  a captured specific sport need does not also require an equivalent category label. A new sport
  mentioned in the conversation is still missing if the candidate records only a surface.
  An explicitly stated intended use that already names the activity (e.g. primary_use=Sprinting)
  captures that activity; do not demand an additional sport=sprinting claim for the same fact.
  A road surface alone, however, does not establish road running rather than walking.
- Labels must cover ALL current schema-defined intent established by the visible USER conversation,
  including unambiguous implications. Do not invent constraints from persona background, a matching
  catalog entry, or an assistant's suggestion. Retire task claims on completion; retain durable claims.

rollout.extractor_prompt:
Extract current intent using only the visible two-way conversation and schema.
Return intent as a short natural-language string summarizing the current user goal.
For example: "Find suitable listings matching the current requirements." It must agree with the structured claims
and search request. Update this summary from the latest turn; do not carry an earlier search goal
forward unchanged after completion. In particular:
- "I didn't find what I wanted, so I'll stop searching" => "The user rejected the results and
  stopped searching without finding what they wanted." active_task_id=null, claims contain no task
  requirements, search_request=null, satisfied=false; retain any previously identified selected_products.
- "I found what I wanted, I'm done" => summarize satisfied completion, not an ongoing search.
- Rejecting results while asking to keep looking is NOT completion; summarize the continuing search.
Never use an imperative summary like "Find suitable listings" for a task the user has stopped.
Return all active hard requirements and soft preferences, keeping task and durable scope separate.
Use task-1 for the first search task, task-2 for the next, and so on. Use null when no task is active.
Scope may be unknown when not established. Durable and unknown-scope claims have null task_id.
Resolve confirmations and product references using assistant context, but never treat an assistant suggestion alone as user evidence.
Preserve unrelated requirements when revising a value. Clear temporary requirements at task boundaries. A statement such as "I've found exactly what I
wanted; I'm finished looking" closes the task: active_task_id=null, task claims removed,
selected_products retains the identified product. Preserve durable preferences. Mere politeness is not necessarily completion.
Choosing a product alone does NOT close the search task. For "I'll take the second one", keep
active_task_id=task-1 and existing task claims with task_id=task-1, set selected_products to a list containing the chosen
ID, search_request=null, and satisfied="unk". Only a later expressed completion clears active_task_id
and task-scoped claims. Never output active_task_id=null while retaining task-scoped claims.
Represent a product choice only as selected_products; do not infer all its attributes as durable preferences.
Cite real message IDs in evidence; include the assistant question/list when necessary, and the user's support.
Return value as the actual typed scalar or membership array, never as JSON encoded inside a string. Use schema operators and units.
Also extract satisfied as true for expressed success, false for expressed failure, or "unk" when
not established (including silence). Do not infer satisfaction just from recommendations or selection.
selected_products is the list of catalog IDs the user explicitly chose; [] if unspecified.
Discussing or liking an item alone is not a selection.
Retain that product through task completion. Reset both
outcome fields when a new task begins. Never invent a product because the user says "found it".
The previous prediction is fallible: correct it using the conversation if necessary.
Also emit search_request as part of the intent: {query, filters, preferences}.
query must be a useful, nonempty natural-language search phrase naming the item
category and known needs. Refine the phrase as more needs become known. Never output placeholders such as "/", "*", or schema field names alone. filters contain ALL active hard requirements;
preferences contain soft preferences, never hard filters. Each uses attribute/operator/typed value.
Use the current task's value when it overrides a durable preference on the same attribute. Unknown
scope or strength stays in claims for clarification, not in automatic search constraints.
Return null if there is no active task or a product has already been selected. Selection lookup is
not a new catalog search. Never put unsupported constraints into query text. Emit active claims only, not superseded values. No private plan or expected states are available.
Also return target_products as the list of catalog IDs the USER explicitly expressed interest in.
Assistant recommendations alone never establish interest. Add IDs after an explicit expression
of interest; remove IDs when the user withdraws interest. Selecting an item also expresses interest.
Keep selected_products separate: interest alone is not a selection and does not stop search.
Resolve positions using the assistant's actual displayed order. Use [] when no interest or selection
has been expressed. Keep selections within target_products. Reset both lists when a new task begins.
Also return preferences as a list of {preferred: catalog_ID, over: catalog_ID} pairs.
"I prefer X over Y" means X > Y. "I prefer X" in an unambiguous displayed comparison
means X > each of the other compared alternatives. Resolve the comparison set from the
user's reference and assistant context; do not compare against every item ever shown.
"I like X" alone establishes interest, not relative preference. A comparison request alone
establishes neither. Preference adds X to target_products but does not select X or reject Y.
Do NOT add Y to target_products merely because it is compared or liked LESS than X.
A request to compare X and Y alone does NOT add either to target_products.
Keep Y as a target only if the user separately expressed interest in Y.
Preserve earlier pairs, replace a reversed pair when the user revises it, and reset preferences
on a new task. Do not invent transitive pairs or infer durable attribute preferences.
Intent contract:
- Attribute requirements and durable attribute preferences belong in claims. An attribute preference
  (e.g. generally preferring a brand or work arrangement) NEVER creates an item-to-item ranking.
- target_products is an explicitly endorsed shortlist of catalog ENTRY IDs, not all eligible items.
  Asking for a comparison, mentioning a model, or requiring its attributes does not endorse an entry,
  even if only one catalog entry currently matches. Catalog descriptions alone establish no user facts.
- selected_products requires an explicit choice of a catalog entry, not mere liking or preference.
  Selection alone neither completes a task nor establishes satisfaction.
- preferences contains only directed {preferred: catalog-entry-ID, over: catalog-entry-ID} pairs.
  "I prefer the first one" after a clear comparison ranks it above the other compared entries.
  It endorses that entry without selecting it or rejecting the others. Attribute values are never IDs.
- Withdrawing interest removes only the identified entry from the shortlist/selection. It does not
  retract a model, brand or other attribute requirement unless the user separately says so. Wording
  must distinguish a particular listing from the model or class of items. New tasks reset item state.
- satisfied describes the overall task outcome: true for explicit overall success, false for explicit
  overall failure, and "unk" if not established. Rejecting one recommendation while continuing the
  search does not by itself establish an overall failure. Never infer an outcome from assistant tone.
- Do not require redundant re-encodings of the same fact in additional_intent. For example,
  a captured specific sport need does not also require an equivalent category label. A new sport
  mentioned in the conversation is still missing if the candidate records only a surface.
  An explicitly stated intended use that already names the activity (e.g. primary_use=Sprinting)
  captures that activity; do not demand an additional sport=sprinting claim for the same fact.
  A road surface alone, however, does not establish road running rather than walking.
- Labels must cover ALL current schema-defined intent established by the visible USER conversation,
  including unambiguous implications. Do not invent constraints from persona background, a matching
  catalog entry, or an assistant's suggestion. Retire task claims on completion; retain durable claims.
